questions.prompt: What is a population in ecology?
options: A group of the same species in one area
questions.explanation: A population is a group of organisms of the SAME species living in the same place at the same time.
questions.misconception: Mixed species together form a community, not a population - populations are one species.

options: When births and arrivals outnumber deaths and departures
questions.explanation: A population grows when more members are added (births, arrivals) than are lost (deaths, departures).
questions.misconception: Growth is about the balance of gains and losses, not just one event.

questions.prompt: Which can limit how large a population grows?
questions.explanation: Food, water, space, disease, and predators all act as limits on population size.
questions.misconception: Limits are about real resources and threats, not appearance or labels.

questions.prompt: Which comes just above population in the ecological hierarchy?
questions.explanation: The order is organism -> population -> community -> ecosystem. Different populations together form a community.
questions.misconception: Communities sit above populations; organism is the level below.
